meta.note: Simulated crew from published ranges. Not real astronaut data.

hr.label: Resting heart rate
hr.explain: Fluid shifts toward the head and less work against gravity change how the heart works in space. A resting rate that drifts from your normal can signal fatigue, dehydration, illness or cardiovascular deconditioning.
hr.how_to_measure: Seated, after 5 minutes of rest, first thing in the morning. Use the wrist monitor or count your pulse for 60 seconds.

actions.amber: Re-measure tonight at rest. Check hydration and sleep. Avoid heavy exercise until it settles.
actions.red: Stop strenuous activity, re-measure in 15 min, and contact the flight surgeon.

bp_sys.label: Systolic blood pressure
bp_sys.explain: Blood pressure changes as fluids redistribute in microgravity and after returning to gravity. A sustained rise above your own baseline deserves attention.
bp_sys.how_to_measure: Cuff on the upper arm, seated and still, arm at heart level. Take two readings 1 minute apart and log the average.

actions.amber: Repeat the measurement tonight. Review salt and fluid intake.
actions.red: Repeat now. If it's still high, contact the flight surgeon.

bp_dia.label: Diastolic blood pressure
bp_dia.explain: The pressure in your arteries between heartbeats. It's read together with systolic pressure.

glucose.label: Blood glucose (fasting)
glucose.explain: Spaceflight can reduce insulin sensitivity. Tracking fasting glucose helps spot metabolic changes and diet issues early.

actions.amber: Review meals and exercise for the last 2 days. Re-test tomorrow morning.
actions.red: If below 60: take fast sugar now and re-test in 15 min. If above 180: contact the flight surgeon.

temp.label: Body temperature
temp.explain: Core temperature tends to run slightly higher in space. A jump above your baseline can be an early sign of infection, since the immune system changes in flight.
temp.how_to_measure: Thermometer under the tongue or in the ear, at rest.

actions.amber: Re-measure in 4 hours and watch for symptoms.
actions.red: Isolate if possible, hydrate, and contact the flight surgeon.

sleep_h.label: Sleep
sleep_h.explain: Light-dark cycles, noise and workload disrupt sleep in space. Chronic short sleep hurts mood, reaction time and mission safety.
sleep_h.how_to_measure: Log the hours slept, or sync your wearable each morning.

actions.amber: Protect tonight's sleep window: dim lights and no screens 1 h before bed. Ask for a lighter schedule tomorrow if needed.
actions.red: Flag to the commander and flight surgeon. Avoid safety-critical tasks.

mood.label: Mood (1–5)
mood.explain: Isolation and confinement are among the five hazards of spaceflight. A downward trend in self-rated mood is an early signal worth acting on.

actions.amber: Schedule a private call home or a crew social activity. Try the guided breathing module.
actions.red: Book a private conference with the flight psychologist.

exercise_min.label: Exercise
exercise_min.explain: Without gravity, bones and muscles weaken quickly. Daily resistance and aerobic exercise is the main countermeasure.
exercise_min.how_to_measure: Logged automatically by the exercise devices, or entered manually.

actions.amber: Make up the missed volume over the next 2 days, prioritising resistance work.
actions.red: Talk to the strength coach today: bone loss risk is rising.

bone_loss_pct.label: Estimated bone loss
bone_loss_pct.explain: An estimate of cumulative loss in bone mineral density at weight-bearing sites, driven by mission days and exercise compliance.
bone_loss_pct.how_to_measure: Estimated from mission day and exercise logs. Confirmed with scans when available.

actions.amber: Increase resistance exercise and check calcium and vitamin D intake.

dose_mSv_day.label: Radiation dose (daily)
dose_mSv_day.explain: Measured by your personal dosimeter. It jumps during solar radiation storms.

actions.amber: Limit time outside shielded areas today.
actions.red: Go to the storm shelter now. Postpone all EVAs.

dose_mSv_cum.label: Radiation dose (mission total)
dose_mSv_cum.explain: Your total dose so far, compared against NASA's career limit.
dose_mSv_cum.how_to_measure: Sum of your daily dosimeter readings.

actions.amber: Review the EVA plan with the flight surgeon.
actions.red: Career limit reached: no further exposure allowed.
